title: PRD: Interleaved Endpoint Mode (chat + embeddings + rerank) - Acceptance & Launch Runbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This PRD defines a new hosted API mode — Interleaved Endpoint Mode (IEM) — that allows a single request to express a mixed interaction: natural-language chat plus one or more on-the-fly embeddings for retrieval signals and an optional rerank step over a returned candidate set. IEM aims to reduce round-trips for composite flows (chat+retrieve+rank) while preserving the behavioral guarantees of existing endpoints.
background_and_rationale: Many Redwood customers build retrieval-augmented generation flows and currently orchestrate three separate calls (embed -> retrieve -> generate) or use a multi-call hub. This increases end-to-end latency and increases token/compute cost due to repeated context serialization. IEM provides an official hosted surface for composing these operations server-side with explicit control over quality vs cost tradeoffs and observable per-step telemetry.
goals: Provide a single hosted API contract that composes generation, embeddings, and rerank without requiring customers to manage orchestration.
Keep median end-to-end P95 latency within 1.5x of plain chat for light-weight rerank paths under typical traffic profiles.
Expose safety and deterministic behavior hooks so customers can rely on acceptance tests and evals during rollout.
Offer clear cost/quality knobs (batching window, quantization profile, rerank depth) surfaced in the Console.
non_goals: Replacing advanced custom retrieval systems or building a full vector DB inside Redwood (we will integrate with customer DBs via connectors).
Guaranteeing identical output to customer-side orchestration for non-deterministic generation when any model sampling is enabled.
user_stories: As an ML engineer, I want to call a single endpoint for chat+retrieve so my client does fewer network hops and has a simpler retry model.
As a product manager, I want telemetry that attributes cost and latency per logical step (embed / retrieve / rerank / generate) so I can analyze unit economics.
As a platform engineer, I want rollout controls to disable rerank or switch to a cheaper model variant during capacity pressure.
api_contract_summary: New endpoint: POST /v1/interleaved_interaction with payload fields: 'messages' (chat), 'embed_inputs' (optional list of texts), 'rerank' (optional object with 'candidate_limit' and 'model'), and 'routing' (optional: 'latency', 'cost', 'regional'). Response contains 'steps' array with typed outputs (embedding_vectors, candidate_ids, generation) and per-step diagnostics. Streaming supported with top-level events 'step_start'|'step_end'|'token'.
behavioral_contracts: Determinism: If request sets deterministic: true and model supports deterministic seed, entire composed flow will attempt determinism; however retrieval and external connectors may introduce variance.

Fallbacks: If an optional step fails (e.g., external DB timeout) then behavior follows configured policy: 'fail'|'partial'|'skip_rerank'. Defaults to 'partial' which returns best-effort generation with warnings in diagnostics.
Quota/Rate-limit: embed and generate tokens are billed as usual; rerank is billed per candidate evaluated. Customers must opt-in to high-depth rerank to avoid surprise bills.
operational_requirements: Per-request tracing that ties tokens to the selected model variant and kernel path.
Telemetry: per-step latency histograms, QPS per step, token distribution, and cost attribution visible in Console and exportable to BigQuery.
Runtime feature gates for canary rollouts and dynamic rerank depth toggles.
Integration hooks for VPC/private connectors to fetch external candidate sets securely.
acceptance_criteria: API contract implemented and validated by contract tests against a canonical client harness (see test-harness PR #425 on GitHub).
End-to-end median latency for recommended default config <= 1.5x plain chat for 95% of sampled production traffic profiles (validated in staging).
Per-step telemetry surfaces in Console with cost attribution and example dashboards prebuilt.
Fallback policies documented and verified through simulated connector failures in Chaos environment with no data leaks.
Security review completed and signed-off (SRE/Security) for VPC connector paths and key handling.
launch_strategy: Phased rollout: alpha -> closed beta -> public GA. Alpha (internal + 2 customers) with rerank disabled by default. Closed beta (10 customers) to exercise rerank and external connector cases. GA opens to self-serve with opt-in pricing for rerank depth > 50 candidates.
rollout_safety_gates: SLOs: 99.9% endpoint success rate during beta; degrade to 'best-effort' mode automatically if success drops below 99% for 10m.
Quality: no more than 1% of sampled outputs flagged by eval suite as regression vs baseline generation quality across a representative eval set.
Cost: early adopter accounts must accept explicit rerank billing confirmation; any unexpected >2x cost variance triggers automated throttle.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Interleaved - Per-step latency + error rates, cost per request, model variant distribution.
Alerts: P95 latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes, per-step error rate > 1%, unknown connector failures > 0.5%.
Runbook: If rerank subsystem causes latency spikes, toggle rerank to 'skip' via feature flag and open priority incident (ENG oncall).
console_and_ui_requirements: Console will show a new Interleaved Endpoint flow in the Deployments page: configuration toggles for rerank depth, embed model choice, regional routing, and a 'simulate' panel that runs cost and latency estimates for the chosen config.
billing_and_pricing_notes: Base per-token billing applies to generation and embeddings. Rerank billed per candidate evaluated with tiered price breaks. Early beta promotional credits will cover rerank charges for invited customers.
security_requirements: Credentials for external connectors must never be stored in plain text; KMS integration required.
Auditable logs for connector requests and responses preserved in customer-controlled storage when VPC mode is enabled.
Threat model review to cover potential exfiltration via candidate payloads.
testing_plan: Unit and integration tests for the API contract and per-step error handling (ENG PRs link in artifacts).
Performance tests: synthetic traces for 1k requests/sec interleaved patterns with varying candidate limits.
Eval regression suite: run against curated prompt set used by Hosted Endpoint QA team with threshold alerts.
Chaos tests: simulate network, DB connector, and model node failures and verify fallback policies.
migration_and_compatibility: No breaking changes to existing chat/completion endpoints. Customers can adopt IEM gradually; migration guide includes code samples for converting two-call retrieve->generate to a single IEM call and cost comparison examples.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected high bills from deep rerank usage. Mitigation: require explicit opt-in and a hard cap per account during beta.
Risk: Increased tail latency when rerank is enabled. Mitigation: fast-path rerank (cheap model) and ability to disable rerank via routing policy automatically.
Risk: Data leakage with external connectors. Mitigation: VPC-only connector option + mandatory KMS encryption + security review.
